short: Attention pooling of the lip map (M06) was ahead in 2021 but not the route to later SOTA; WordPiece output (M08) was preceded by BPE in 2020; the SOTA table mixes data budgets.
position: The paper [@prajwal2022] changes the visual front-end (M06) and the output unit (M08) of sentence-level lip reading. Attention pooling over a 24x24 feature map was ahead in October 2021: earlier lip-reading uses of spatial attention fused streams or sat inside a ResNet that still averaged (Appendix), and the gain holds on LRS2 WER (37.2 to 30.9%) and on speech-detection mAP (80.2 to 88.2). It did not become the route to the state of the art: the lowest [later] LRS3 WER, 12.8%, uses a linear-projection front-end on 100,000 hours, and the best public-data systems keep ResNet-18 trunks and gain from data and semi-supervision; within its own generation VTP beat the ResNet plus Conformer baseline. WordPiece output is not new, since byte-pair outputs were used for LRS2 a year earlier, so the claim of first use is wrong, though the 41.0 to 37.2% ablation is a clean gain. The state-of-the-art claim rests on systems trained on 389 to 31,000 hours, with no seeds or repeated runs and unstated WER normalisation.
